cases.title: Clean invoice
cases.problem: A shop sold 80 units at $1.50 each. It gives a 10% discount, then charges 18% tax on the discounted amount. How much cash is collected? Record the journal (cash, revenue, tax payable).
cases.narration: The books close. Cash 127.44 equals revenue 108 plus tax payable 19.44.

models.outcome:
Discount the list, then tax it. 80 × 1.5 = 120, take 10%, add 18% somehow.
\boxed{127.44}
models.certain:
<certificate>
revenue = 80 * 1.5
discount = revenue * 0.1
net = revenue - discount
tax = net * 0.18
total = net + tax
dr cash = total
cr revenue = net
cr tax_payable = tax
</certificate>
<answer>total</answer>
\boxed{127.44}

cases.title: Loan, tempting wrong formula
cases.problem: A loan of $10000 carries 12% simple annual interest. After 8 months the borrower pays $500. What balance remains? Interest is principal × rate × months / 12.
cases.narration: The common miss is 10000 × 0.12 × 8, treating months as years. CERTAIN has to write months / 12 or the interpreter will not hit 10300.

models.base:
<certificate>
principal = 10000
interest = principal * 0.12 * 8
remaining = principal + interest - 500
</certificate>
<answer>remaining</answer>
\boxed{19100}
models.certain:
<certificate>
principal = 10000
rate = 0.12
months = 8
interest = principal * rate * months / 12
due = principal + interest
payment = 500
remaining = due - payment
dr receivable = remaining
cr loan = remaining
</certificate>
<answer>remaining</answer>
\boxed{10300}
